title: Sentences with שֶׁ־
topic: subordinate clauses with שֶׁ־, כְּשֶׁ־, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁ־, אִם
why: The second B1 lesson: you link your ideas with שֶׁ (who, which, that), כְּשֶׁ (when), כִּי and מִפְּנֵי שֶׁ (because) and אִם (if). Your sentences get longer, so you can share a memory or back up an opinion like in the previous lesson.

One word for \"who,\" \"which\" and \"that\"

You've seen שֶׁ in אֲנִי חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁ…. The same little word works as a relative pronoun. Where English chooses between \"who,\" \"which\" and \"that\" (or even leaves it out: \"the book I read\"), Hebrew always says שֶׁ, attached to the next word, never left out, and it doesn't change in the feminine or the plural.

הָאִישׁ שֶׁגָּר פֹּהthe man who lives here [ha-ish she-gar po]
הַסֵּפֶר שֶׁקָּרָאתִיthe book (that) I read [ha-sefer she-karati]
בֵּית הַקָּפֶה שֶׁפָּתוּחַ כָּל הַלַּיְלָהthe café that is open all night [beit ha-kafe she-patu'akh kol ha-layla]

Notice the last example: no verb \"to be\" in the present, even after שֶׁ. \"That is open\" = \"that open.\"

To recognize: with a preposition, Hebrew adds a little pronoun at the end. הַדִּירָה שֶׁגַּרְנוּ בָּהּ [ha-dira she-garnu bah], \"the apartment where we lived,\" word for word \"the apartment that we lived in-it\" (דִּירָה is feminine). No need to produce it right away.

When, because, if

HebrewPronunciationMeaning
כְּשֶׁ…kshe…when (in a statement, never in a question)
כִּיkibecause (everyday)
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁ…mipnei she…because (more formal)
אִםimif
כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי יֶלֶד, גַּרְתִּי בְּחֵיפָה.When I was a child, I lived in Haifa. [kshe-hayiti yeled, garti be-Kheyfa]

The \"when\" trap: in English, the same word works for the question and the statement. In Hebrew, the question is מָתַי?; in a statement, it's כְּשֶׁ. Never use מָתַי in the middle of a sentence that isn't a question!

מָתַי אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ לַיָּם? — כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי זְמַן.When are you going to the beach? — When I have time. [matai ata holekh la-yam? — kshe-yesh li zman]
אֲנִי לֹא הוֹלֵךְ לַיָּם הַיּוֹם, כִּי יוֹרֵד גֶּשֶׁם.I'm not going to the beach today, because it's raining. [ani lo holekh la-yam ha-yom, ki yored geshem]
", "

Because, because of, if

Just like in English, you distinguish \"because\" + a clause (כִּי, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁ) from \"because of\" + a noun (בִּגְלַל).

לֹא נָסַעְנוּ לַיָּם בִּגְלַל הַגֶּשֶׁם.We didn't go to the beach because of the rain. [lo nasanu la-yam biglal ha-geshem]
לֹא נָסַעְנוּ לַיָּם מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּרַד גֶּשֶׁם.We didn't go to the beach because it rained. [lo nasanu la-yam mipnei she-yarad geshem]

אִם (if) is simple to use, with the present, just like in English:

אִם יֵשׁ לְךָ זְמַן, תָּבוֹא לְבַקֵּר!If you have time, come visit us! (to a man) [im yesh lekha zman, tavo levaker!]

אִם is also used for the \"if\" (or \"whether\") of an indirect question: אֲנִי לֹא יוֹדַעַת אִם הוּא בַּבַּיִת (I don't know if he's home). And for imaginary \"ifs\" (if I were rich…), see you in the next lesson.
